filename: Interactive Atmospheric Composition Emulation for Next-Generation Earth System Models.pdf
title: Interactive Atmospheric Composition Emulation for Next-Generation Earth System Models
venue: NeurIPS 2025 Workshop on Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning
parameterization_target: interactive atmospheric black carbon aerosol transport and concentrations (BCB)
testbed_rationale: The paper uses NASA GISS-ModelE3 simulations to train a ConvLSTM-based emulator for 3D black carbon transport, but provides no data or code availability statements or links, making the data currently inaccessible for benchmarking.
pain_points: Memory and computational bottleneck loading numerous 2D and 3D ESM variables at high temporal resolution (30-min intervals).
Orders-of-magnitude decrease in aerosol concentrations with altitude causes global normalization strategies to bias loss functions towards lower atmospheric levels.
Autoregressive rollout errors in standard models, necessitating spatio-temporal architectures to handle long-range dependencies.
Underestimation of extreme wildfire events not well represented in historical training data (e.g., extreme 2020/2021 wildfire seasons in the Western US).
extraction_notes: The paper describes 'Smart NINT', an ML emulator designed to run interactively in ModelE to replace non-interactive tracer (NINT) climatologies, but the evaluation in this paper is offline.
